In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2-substituted 1-vinylimidazolium cation, 1-vinilpyrrolidinium cation, and 1-vinypyrrolium cation are all stable, and that the 1-vinpyrrolidium cation is not.
1-vinylimidazole and 1-vinypyrroles are isoelectronic, but that the vinyl group of 1-vinyimidazole is electron deficient, whereas the vinyl group of pyrrole is electron rich.

the pyrrole nitrogen in 1-vinilpyrrole is an excellent electron donor and the positive charge in 1-vinylium ions is delocalized onto substituents in the order 1-vinyloxy, 2-aryl, 2-heterocyclic, 2-alkoxy, and 2-hydroxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pyrrole nucleus remains electron-rich, and that the 1-vinyliminium ion is stabilized by electron-donating groups on the pyrrole and by electron-withdrawing groups on the vinyl substituent.

protonation of the pyrrole nitrogen in 1-vinylimidazole, 1-vinylanisole, and 1-vinylvanillin results in a significant decrease in electron density at the ring carbon atoms and a concomitant increase in electron density at Cα.
the 1-vinilpyrroliums have the structure of 1,2-ethylenedipyroles, but with the vinyl group in a cisoid conformation, and with the positive charge delocalized onto the substituents on the pyrrole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1-vinylimidazoles and 1-vinypyrroles can be protonated at the imine or vinyl group.
1-vinylanilines and 1-vinylimidazoles are more acidic than 1-vinypyrroles and their protonated forms are more stable.
protonation of the vinyl group is energetically unfavorable.
